findings.scenario: A completed attempt with a schema-valid unapplied proposal satisfies both the generic success rule (`active -> terminal`: output settles the segment) and the proposal-HITL gate. Input: attemptIndex 0 is `completed` with typed proposal P, segment still `active`, no live handle. A worker CASes `active -> completed` on `stateRevision` and emits a completed receipt with P, never writing interrupt/proposal/expected-state hashes. Wrong behavior: proposal-HITL is skipped entirely (or lost to a race with `active -> interrupted`); unique CAS binding, live gates, accept/cancel terminals, and the human decision never run; P can still enter the guarded apply flow as a completed-segment proposal. That silently invalidates every Proposal-HITL guarantee.
findings.remediation: Close a mutex: when the current attempt is `completed` with a schema-valid unapplied proposal, forbid `active -> completed|failed|budget-exhausted`. Allow only `active -> interrupted` (proposal-HITL) or operational `active -> cancelled`. Add an S2 oracle that a typed proposal cannot obtain a completed segment receipt without the interrupt CAS and a unique `accept-proposal` decision.

findings.line: RouteSegmentStateV1 hash fields; 'Every segment transition is a compare-and-swap on stateRevision'; '`interrupted` requires all four...'
findings.scenario: The four interrupt/proposal/expected-state hashes are required in `interrupted` and compared on the way out, but they are optional fields and are not declared write-once. The general rule is a `stateRevision` CAS; listed transitions are only enum changes; `interrupted -> interrupted` is unstated. Input: segment is `interrupted` bound to interrupt H1 and proposal P1; a later `stateRevision` CAS keeps `state=interrupted` and replaces `pendingProposalEnvelopeHash`/`interruptHash`/expected-state hashes with P2/H2. Wrong behavior: the human accepts H1/P1 while the bound CAS record now names P2, so unique interrupt/proposal/expected-state binding does not hold for the life of the gate.
findings.remediation: Make the four hashes write-once at `active -> interrupted` and immutable until a listed `interrupted -> completed|cancelled` CAS. Forbid any CAS that remains in `interrupted`. Accept/cancel must compare the original four hashes plus `stateRevision`; any mismatch cancels.

audit.proof_assessment: HEAD equals BASE; the only artifact is this planning contract. The attached Grok interrupt-reconcile FINDINGS describe bytes that are not in this file (`interrupted -> active`, RouteSegmentStateV1 without interrupt/proposal/expected-state hashes, terminal-only quarantine). Those findings are not authority for OBX-P180-S2-PROPOSAL-HITL. Current text does distinguish proposal-HITL from cancel/switch, requires a completed attempt and no live handle, stores the four hashes, terminals on accept/cancel, checks live gates on accept, quarantines late output while interrupted, and denies apply on accept. Remaining criterion holes are the still-open `active -> completed` path beside HITL and non-immutability of the interrupted hash bindings.
residual_risks: Atomic CAS is specified across segment, settled attempt, interrupt, and reservation records with no single closed record; in-memory fixtures cannot prove durable atomicity.
S2 references a unique accept-proposal decision/slot but RouteSegmentStateV1 has no decisionHash; uniqueness depends on later S3 slot CAS.
`no attempt may be retryable-failure` fail-closes proposal-HITL after a successful index-1 retry while attempt 0 remains `retryable-failure`.
interrupted -> completed requires the reservation still held but never reconciles/releases it, so accept can leak budget.
Leftover 'Resume or cancellation' wording can be misread as interrupted -> active despite that transition being absent.
